statement: Micron committed $500 million to GlobalWafers' Texas plant under a 10-year supply agreement, within a raised $250 billion U.S. spending plan targeting 40% U.S.-based DRAM output by 2035
why: A prepayment and a decade-long lock-in are what buyers do when they expect the input to stay scarce.

impact.mechanism: Prepaid long-term wafer capacity secures memory makers' feedstock and funds new supply, but the relief arrives only as the new capacity comes online.

evidence.excerpt: GlobalWafers signed a 10-year supply agreement with Micron (the longest such contract in wafer-industry history) starting next year, including a $500 million prepayment

confidence.basis: Secondary outlet plus a wire summary of the same underlying story; no company filing consulted.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: Tom's Hardware
